name: Businesses priced off Starship launch costs
title: Space businesses priced off Starship: no-go until it is measured
question: Can you build a space business priced off Starship's launch costs yet?
answer: Many space business plans assume launch below $200 per kilogram once Starship flies commercially. That is a target, not a price anyone can buy today. The last measured step was Falcon 9, which NASA put at about $2,720/kg advertised. Until third parties buy Starship launches at a published price, a plan priced off it is priced off a forecast.
verdict_reason: No one can buy launch at the assumed price yet; announced is not measured.

constraint.name: Measured, purchasable launch price
constraint.detail: Vendor targets lead measured prices by years; only a price third parties pay counts as a crossing.

metric.label: Cost to launch one kilogram to low Earth orbit (NASA estimate, 2018)
metric.note: Two points from one NASA paper: Space Shuttle (first flight 1981) at about $54,500/kg and Falcon 9 (first flight 2010) at its advertised $2,720/kg. Advertised prices are list prices, not audited costs.

graveyard_note: The relevant graveyard is historical (Teledesic, Iridium) and lives on their pages. This entry is a warning against pricing off announced numbers.

evidence.text: NASA estimate: Falcon 9 advertised $2,720/kg to LEO.
